req.title: Delete only by author
req.statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 403 Forbidden when a user attempts to delete a post they did not author.

doc.reasoning: The requirement states that only the author of a post may delete it; any other authenticated user attempting to delete a post they did not author must receive HTTP 403. Three test cases are designed: (1) Positive – the actual author successfully deletes their own post (EP, verifies the happy path and that the 403 guard does NOT fire for the author). (2) Negative – a different authenticated user attempts to delete a post they did not author and receives exactly HTTP 403 (NEG + DT, directly targets the authorization check in get_post). (3) Boundary – a user who owns some posts but not the specific target post attempts deletion, exercising the author_id != g.user['id'] boundary condition (BVA + comparison-mutation). All tests use pre-loaded data: post id=7 is authored by user id=2 (Anjali/cloud); user id=1 (Rahul/stone) is a non-author. Post id=2 is authored by user id=1 (Rahul/stone). Tests are self-contained, deterministic, and idempotent.

tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_author_can_delete_own_post():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Rahul', 'password': 'stone'})
    assert r.status_code == 302
    r = client.post('/2/delete')
    assert r.status_code == 302
    assert r.headers['Location'] == '/'

test_author_can_delete_own_post()

tests.name: test_boundary_author_id_mismatch_exactly_403
preconditions: Database pre-loaded with standard fixture rows
Post id=17 is authored by user id=3 (Ishaan)
Anjali (user id=2) is authenticated — adjacent user id, not the author
This exercises the author_id != g.user['id'] comparison at the boundary of adjacent ids (3 vs 2)
actions: POST to /17/delete (post authored by Ishaan, user_id=3; Anjali is user_id=2, one less)
expected: Post id=17 must NOT be deleted (still exists in DB)
trace: R-FLASKR-020: BVA on author_id comparison — adjacent ids (2 vs 3) must still yield 403
blog.delete -> get_post(17, check_author=True) -> post['author_id'](3) != g.user['id'](2) -> abort(403)
Catches mutations that flip != to == or use >= instead of ==

tests.name: test_unauthenticated_delete_redirects_not_403
preconditions: Database pre-loaded with standard fixture rows
No user is logged in (no session cookie)
actions: POST to /2/delete without any prior login
expected: HTTP 302 redirect to /auth/login (login_required fires before authz check)
NOT 403 — unauthenticated state is handled by login_required, not the author check
trace: R-FLASKR-020: state transition — unauthenticated -> redirect (not 403); 403 only applies to authenticated non-authors
STC: covers the state where session has no user_id, distinguishing it from the authenticated-non-author state
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_unauthenticated_delete_redirects_not_403():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.post('/2/delete')
    assert r.status_code == 302
    assert '/auth/login' in r.headers['Location']
    assert r.status_code != 403

test_unauthenticated_delete_redirects_not_403()
